analysis.title: UBS House View - Daily US: Resilient growth should steady markets
key_insights: The 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.34% intraday Thursday, its highest since 2002, then reversed to close about 4 basis points lower at 5.24% after senior Fed officials said they were in no hurry to raise rates again.

UBS expects resilient growth and a more patient Fed to let equities absorb moderately higher rates. It expects equity gains over the next 6 to 12 months and recommends broad sector and regional diversification while managing concentration risk.

Labor data is strong going into the payrolls report. Initial claims fell to 197,000 (lowest in 10 weeks) and continuing claims fell to 1.7 million (lowest in 3.5 years). Consensus for September payrolls is +90,000 with unemployment unchanged at 4.1%, and UBS says a gain in line with that would still be consistent with a healthy labor market.
ISM manufacturing was 54.5 in September with the employment component at 52.7. Prices paid rose to 77.9 against an expected 73.0, which UBS flags as a risk to bond yields.

Three-month annualized core PCE inflation fell to 2.05% in August, the lowest since July 2024. UBS expects further disinflation over the next six months, with a renewed broadening of price pressures as the risk to that view.

Fed officials Jefferson, Bowman and Williams signaled no urgency to hike. Market-implied odds of an October hike fell to about 30% from 70% on Monday. UBS's base case is one more hike in December, then a hold through 2027, rather than the extended tightening cycle priced in markets.
UBS forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth of 25% this year and 14% in 2027, which it says should help equities absorb higher rates.

European sovereign bonds sold off. France's 2027 budget targets a deficit of 5% of GDP versus an estimated 5.4% in 2026, with EUR 43B of new consolidation measures. The French-German 10-year spread widened 14 basis points (largest daily rise since March 2020) and the Italian spread widened 16 basis points (most since July 2022).

German Bunds rallied as ECB tightening expectations eased: the 2-year yield fell 14 basis points to 3.07% and the 10-year fell 8 basis points to 3.51%. European high yield spreads widened 18 basis points and the Stoxx Banks index fell 3.9%.

UBS sees France's budget as a step toward consolidation but expects French bonds to stay sensitive to risk appetite. It sees no imminent funding crisis, citing the limited reaction to the budget and solid demand at the latest auction. It expects one more 25-basis-point ECB hike in December and stays Attractive on fixed income, favoring short- to medium-term maturities, stronger investment grade issuers and select French agency, covered and corporate bonds.

EURUSD fell as low as 1.1214, its weakest since May 2025, down about 1.2% on the week and more than 3% since the start of September. Drivers cited are French fiscal concerns, high US yields, higher energy prices, broad dollar strength and fears the US could limit diesel exports.

UBS sees EURUSD risks skewed toward a recovery and recommends gradually building euro exposure. It expects EURUSD at 1.15-1.20 over the medium term and favors selling EURUSD downside below 1.12 over a one-month horizon.
earnings_insights: UBS forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth of 25% for 2026 and 14% for 2027 (bank forecast, not reported figures).
